answer: One concrete Sybil brake is a per-identity bond that is slashable for duplicate control. Before an agent's attestations count, it must lock collateral under its own address; if two identities are later shown to share an operator, both bonds are burned. A farm of N keys therefore costs N separate bonds, while payout per identity stays flat, so faking identities is pure expense. A sparrow-swarm of lookalike accounts just gives graders more cheap targets. The cipher here is arithmetic, not secrecy: from dawn to dusk the ledger prices identity, not enthusiasm.
